data.title: ChangXin Technology Discusses Long-Term Supply Agreements With Multiple Major Customers
data.description: ChangXin Technology said at its third-quarter 2026 earnings briefing that it has discussed long-term supply agreements with multiple major customers to secure medium- and long-term demand. According to Odaily, the company expects its gross margin to remain stable in the fourth quarter.

data.title: Binance Plans PoR Snapshot by 15:33 (UTC+8) Today, Phased Withdrawal Resumption by 13:33 (UTC+8) Tomorrow
data.description: Binance released Security Incident Update #2 at 3:33 AM on October 31 (UTC+8), disclosing two key upcoming timelines.According to the announcement, the company plans to complete its first Proof of Reserves snapshot within 12 hours of the announcement and publish the results by November 2; meanwhile, the tech team aims to begin resuming withdrawal services in phases within approximately 34 hours. In specific terms, this means completing the snapshot by 15:33 (UTC+8) on October 31 and starting the resumption of withdrawals by 13:33 (UTC+8) on November 1, with actual progress depending on the completion of security checks.Binance previously stated that it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds, of which approximately $5 billion in equivalent impacted token assets are already in place, covering roughly 80% of the stolen assets, with the remainder being purchased through market and OTC channels. In addition, approximately $3 billion of the impacted assets has been frozen on-chain.

data.title: Rip Cars Raises $1.5 Million in Funding With DBA Among Investors
data.description: Rip Cars said it raised $1.5 million, with investors including DBA, Colosseum, Kyle Samani, Novora, Anas Khader, Sacha Saint-Leger and Erik C. According to Odaily, Rip Cars is a Solana-based collectibles platform centered on physical Hot Wheels die-cast cars. Users can open digital card packs backed by real inventory, then hold the cars digitally, redeem them for physical delivery or sell them through the platform’s buyback program.

data.title: TradFi News |TradFi Week in Review: Silver Drops 18% in October, Intel Has Its Worst Day Since 1974, and a 10-2 Fed Hold Keeps a December Hike in Play
data.description: Global markets swung sharply in the week to Friday, October 30. Precious metals fell hard, US tech stocks sold off on worries about AI spending, and the Federal Reserve held rates without ruling out a December hike. Strong US growth and inflation data kept expectations of higher rates in place.Gold and Silver SlumpSpot gold closed Friday at $3,876.89 an ounce, down 6.7% for October, while silver closed at $49.13, down more than 18% for the month. Stronger-than-expected US data reinforced expectations of high interest rates, and rising real rates weighed on both metals, according to the summary. Brent crude found support from Middle East supply risks.Tech Stocks Sell OffThe Nasdaq and S&P 500 fell for a third straight week as enthusiasm for AI trades cooled. The Nasdaq lost 5.3% in October, its worst month since March 2025. Alphabet fell as much as 13% intraday on concerns about capital spending and cash flow, and Intel plunged 28.58% on Friday, its worst day since 1974. Apple closed with a market value of $5.03 trillion, ahead of Nvidia’s $4.93 trillion, to reclaim the title of the world’s most valuable listed company.Fed Holds in a Split VoteThe Federal Reserve voted 10-2 to keep rates unchanged, with two officials favoring a 25 basis point hike. Chair Kevin Warsh said the US economy is growing strongly but inflation has run above target for nearly six years, and future decisions will depend on incoming data. Data released the next day supported the hawkish case: third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate, above the 3.2% forecast, and core PCE inflation rose to 3.1% in September from 3.0%. CME FedWatch shows a 75% chance of a 25 basis point hike in December.AI Spending Under ScrutinyThe cost of building AI infrastructure became a central market concern. Meta announced an equity financing plan of up to $97.5 billion, SpaceX raised about $40 billion through equipment leasing, and Oracle said it expects to need up to $20 billion in outside financing by fiscal 2030. Anthropic publicly filed for an IPO, disclosing revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026 and about $637 billion in long-term computing and infrastructure commitments.Chipmakers Post Strong ResultsAI demand continued to lift chipmaker earnings. SK Hynix’s third-quarter operating profit jumped 632% from a year earlier, and SanDisk’s revenue rose 378% in its first fiscal quarter of 2027. Even so, the week’s sell-off showed investors are focusing more on whether AI spending can turn into real profits and free cash flow.

data.title: Global Central Banks Keep Rates Unchanged as US and European Officials Assess Inflation Risk
data.description: Central banks around the world left interest rates unchanged this week as officials in the US and Europe assessed the risk that high energy prices could fuel inflation, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Rezaei: Iran's Retaliation Would Be More Destructive if War Breaks Out Again
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's Mehr News Agency reported that Supreme National Security Council Secretary Rezaei said in an interview that Iran's defensive capabilities have improved and become significantly stronger and more complete compared with before. He said Iran's offensive capabilities have also increased significantly, and that the destructive power, speed, and ability of its missiles to penetrate enemy air defenses have improved. Rezaei said that if confrontation breaks out again, Iran's response will be stronger, more destructive, and more punitive than before, and the United States and the Israeli regime will suffer greater losses.

data.title: Crypto News | Ansem: Crypto May Have Peaked a Year Before US Stocks, and Bitcoin Could Bottom First if Both Keep Falling
data.description: Crypto may have peaked earlier than the US stock market this cycle, crypto trader Ansem said on Saturday, October 31, in a post shared on X. Because risk appetite this cycle has been driven largely by AI and US stocks, he argued, the two markets may top out at different times. If crypto’s recent rebound is only a counter-trend rally and stocks are just beginning a larger correction, crypto could face another leg down. Even so, Ansem said bitcoin may bottom before the broader stock market if both keep falling. He said he is not certain this scenario will play out and will watch how prices react at key levels.Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025 and is now about 38% below it, while the Nasdaq 100 peaked on October 6 this year and has since fallen more than 7%.

data.title: SoftBank-Backed OPay Suspends Planned NYSE IPO Amid Regulatory Inquiry
data.description: OPay Ltd., a Nigeria-focused payments platform, halted its New York Stock Exchange IPO, which was scheduled to begin trading on Friday, citing a regulatory inquiry, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | South Korean Media: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won Meets OpenAI CEO Sam Altman
data.description: According to Jin10, South Korean media reported that SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won had lunch with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on the 31st. Industry insiders said they discussed cooperation on AI business. The specific content of their talks has not been made public, but they were reportedly believed to have discussed potential cooperation on high-bandwidth memory (HBM) supplies and next-generation AI infrastructure. SK Group has maintained close cooperation with OpenAI, including as a key partner in its large-scale AI infrastructure project, Stargate.

data.title: HKT Agrees to Halt U.S. Operations Under FCC Pressure
data.description: According to CNBC, HKT agreed Friday to halt its U.S. telecom services under pressure from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). Under a consent decree, HKT must apply within 30 days to discontinue services and stop providing them by September 1, 2027. The FCC had said in October 2025 that it was moving to revoke HKT’s authority to operate in the United States, citing national security concerns and the company’s affiliation with China Unicom, a PCCW shareholder. The agreement means the FCC will not proceed with the revocation process.

data.title: Stellar Becomes MetaMask’s Default Network, Automatically Generating Addresses for Accounts
data.description: Stellar is now the default network in the MetaMask mobile app and browser extension. According to Odaily, each existing MetaMask account will automatically receive a Stellar address derived from its existing recovery phrase, with no additional setup required. Users can hold, manage, send and receive XLM, Trustline assets and Soroban tokens, and swap between Stellar and other supported networks. Existing Stellar users can also import their accounts using a recovery phrase.

data.title: Microsoft Executive: Voluntary Exit Plan Is Not Aimed at Cutting 60,000 Jobs
data.description:
A Microsoft executive said the company’s broad voluntary separation plan is not intended to cut 60,000 jobs. According to Sina Finance, citing IT Home and Business Insider, Microsoft’s CFO Amy Hood said in an internal memo that the plan gives employees who want to leave the choice to decide how to do so, and that only a “very small number” were expected to accept. Microsoft later said no more than 3,000 employees, or 5% or less of those eligible, were expected to take the offer.

Earlier this year, about one-third of employees accepted a voluntary retirement plan based on age and tenure. Microsoft later conducted layoffs, and some employees who had declined the retirement offer were dismissed. In response to concerns about further cuts, the company said future staffing would depend on business needs and priorities.

Executives said the new plan differs from the earlier one: some departing employees’ roles may be filled by new hires rather than eliminated. Charles Lamanna, who oversees AI, Office and Word, made employees across his departments eligible to apply, with plans to hire for key vacancies. In Microsoft’s Cloud and AI division, the Azure hardware systems and infrastructure team and the cloud operations and innovation team did not participate. Most other teams offered eligibility, and some roles could be refilled.

An executive said replacing senior employees with less-experienced hires could reduce labor costs, but a Microsoft spokesperson said this was not the company’s official position. An anonymous executive also said the plan may address complaints from employees who were ineligible for the earlier offer, and that Microsoft did not intend to cut 60,000 workers or replace everyone with AI.

The U.S. government recently suspended Microsoft’s eligibility for a federal employer sponsorship program that allows companies to sponsor foreign employees seeking U.S. permanent residency. The White House accused Microsoft of laying off U.S. employees while hiring lower-paid foreign workers; Microsoft denied the allegation.

data.title: London Bookmakers’ Losses From US Horse-Race Wagers Remain Unsolved
data.description:
A series of large, unusual wagers on US horse races placed in London saddled some of the city’s betting parlors with hefty losses, and the betting coup remains unsolved, according to Bloomberg.

Lisa Lazarus, the top cop in US horse racing, received calls and emails this summer from UK regulators seeking help after the wagers were placed the previous day.

data.title: Ansem: Crypto May Have Peaked Before U.S. Stocks This Cycle, While Bitcoin Could Bottom First
data.description:
Ansem said crypto markets may already have peaked ahead of U.S. stocks in this cycle. According to ChainCatcher, he said that if the recent rebound is countertrend and U.S. stocks are beginning a broader correction, crypto could face another decline.

Ansem noted that risk appetite in this cycle has been driven largely by AI and the performance of U.S. stocks, making it worth considering whether crypto and traditional markets peaked at different times. He said he was not certain this scenario would unfold and would remain open-minded, watching how both asset classes respond near key price levels.

He added that even if crypto and U.S. stocks continue to fall in the short term, Bitcoin could bottom before the broader stock market.

data.title: STOCKS | AI Spending Pushes Shareholder Returns at Five U.S. Tech Giants to 15-Year Low; Buybacks Fall 83%
data.description:
The shareholder-return ratio at five U.S. tech giants has fallen to a 15-year low amid AI spending, while their buybacks have been cut by 83%. According to Sina Finance, citing Reuters, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle devoted 9.3% of cash generated by their businesses to dividends and buybacks in the first three quarters of this year, down from 27.4% a year earlier; operating cash flow rose 29% to a record $542.9 billion.

Their capital expenditures doubled to $556.9 billion, exceeding the cash flow the companies had generated since data became available in 2011. Their combined free cash flow swung to a $14 billion deficit from a $143.5 billion surplus a year earlier. Buybacks fell to $13.6 billion from $81.8 billion a year earlier.

Alphabet and Meta have made no buybacks so far in 2026, after repurchasing $66.5 billion of shares in the first nine months of last year. Amazon pays no dividend and has not repurchased shares since 2022. Microsoft accounted for nearly all of the five companies’ remaining buybacks, cutting repurchases in its September quarter to $4.4 billion from $5.7 billion a year earlier.

Amazon’s third-quarter capital expenditure was $75.9 billion, nearly 80% more than the $42.4 billion it generated from operations, and it raised $48.1 billion in long-term debt during the quarter. Alphabet also had negative free cash flow and raised about $12.4 billion through share sales and $29 billion through debt issuance.

Ellen Stanhope, co-head of investment management at Franklin Templeton, said companies had increasingly returned surplus capital to shareholders through buybacks and dividends over the past 15 years. She said the current trend may involve increasing equity and debt issuance as a way to seek funds from investors.

data.title: ICE Deletes Trade.xyz Partnership Tweet but Keeps Promotional Repost
data.description: ICE's official account has deleted a post about its partnership with Trade.xyz but still retains a repost of Trade.xyz promotional content. According to Odaily, the companies plan to launch perpetual futures products on Hyperliquid for regulated U.S. markets, subject to regulatory approval. The markets would have separate clearing, customer identity verification and anti-money laundering systems, and the products would be linked to stock indexes, commodities and currency prices.

data.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group’s top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify, Bloomberg reported.
